decisions.summary: The delta is enumerated (research/*.html, SOURCES.html, citations/, the derived .js, this feature's directory, the skill research CLAUDE.md and the root CLAUDE.md, plus the GM's TO-DOWNLOAD.md outside the repository) and the route is DIRECT because no engine code is touched.
decisions.why: FR-014, SC-012 and D3 settle this; the request says nothing about routes and nothing in the enumeration reaches l7r/**/*.py or a pool generator.

decisions.summary: The PAGE is the outer loop and the readers' tier order (HIGH, MEDIUM-HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW-MEDIUM, LOW) runs INSIDE a page, so a MEDIUM item on page 1 is worked before a HIGH item on page 5.
decisions.why: It narrows FR-012's literal whole-list tier order, but SC-010 as accepted admits the departure 'absent a stated reason' and the plan states the reason: record-format and quote-check read a PAGE (FR-007) and the work lands in per-page batches (FR-009), so a strict whole-list tier sweep would leave every page half-noted until the last tier, which is the state FR-009 exists to prevent. The GM's request says nothing about ordering, so nothing is carved out contrary to what was asked, and the purpose of FR-012 - meet the readers' strongest items first - survives inside every page.

decisions.summary: The per-page work list is derived by measure/worklist.py, which imports the census's own parsers so the list is the FR-001 filter applied to one page, ordered by tier, with the quoted sentence located in the page HTML.
decisions.why: FR-001 requires a derived list rather than a restated one; this is the derivation.

decisions.summary: The twenty-two feature-238 R7 closures are recognized when met (a sentence already carrying a footnote mark, or one of the named R7 items) and skipped with a note in research.md.
decisions.why: FR-001 subtracts exactly the R7 classes; skipping a closure when it is met is that subtraction performed.

decisions.summary: An item the harness cannot locate is placed by hand from the reader's section heading.
decisions.why: It adds work rather than removing it, so it narrows nothing. Noted as stale rather than as a narrowing: spec D7, added in the 2026-09-14 split amendment, now sends the 32 unlocatable items on the sixteen landed pages to feature 250 instead, and the plan's P1 was not restated to match. The deferral itself lives in the spec (D7 discloses it as the session's addition, not the GM's, and says it is raised to them with the closing report), so it is the spec track's to carry, not a decision this plan makes.

decisions.summary: The reading is dispatched as parallel background source-reader agents on Opus, eight to twelve claims each, one page at a time, each claim verbatim with its section heading, returning READ with the verbatim passage and the registry material, NOT-FOUND with what was searched, or CONTRADICTED with the quote.
decisions.why: FR-003 requires a source-reader pass before any note is written and the note written from the returned quotes; this is the dispatch shape, and the project's own doctrine puts these agents in the background on Opus.

decisions.summary: Per verdict: a registry key with both write-ups for a new key, the note on the citations page in the citation form with the passage quoted (a foreign-language passage in English translation, marked, with the original after), the mark at the sentence, the key added to the section's roster; an absence note in FR-004's exact form for NOT-FOUND; the sentence rewritten and the correction recorded for CONTRADICTED; new keys to source-applicability before the page's commit.
decisions.why: FR-004, FR-005, FR-006 and FR-007 each carry one clause of this, and the translation rule is the standing project rule rather than a new decision.

decisions.summary: A GROUNDS note is written only for a worked sentence carrying no claim about how a place was built, farmed, planted, governed or lived in and not a labeled guess about the physical world, naming one or more of FR-004's six reasons, and never for a sentence FR-004 bars from the form.
decisions.why: It restates FR-004's closed list and both prohibitions without widening either.

decisions.summary: The per-page check set before that page's commit: make citations; make test-file over the three interactive test files; quote-check and record-format in parallel over the changed page and its citations page; the entry-drift pairs from scripts/_entry_owed.py; then the commit.
decisions.why: FR-005, FR-007, FR-008 and FR-009 name each element; the batching per page is FR-009's own requirement.

decisions.summary: Documents that could not be read go to TO-DOWNLOAD.md Part 4, appended at the END, each with the heading, the guessed direct link, the uniquely identifying Google-search link, what rests on it and what blocked the fetch.
decisions.why: FR-010 as amended, and the GM's 2026-09-14 words in request.md, state exactly these five parts and the append-at-the-end placement.

decisions.summary: The never-searched absence notes are listed by measure/note_census.py --list, worked in the same pipeline AFTER the Phase 1 pages, and counted separately in the closing report.
decisions.why: The GM ruled the never-searched notes in scope (request.md, 2026-09-13); D1 places them after the FR-001 list and FR-011 with SC-013 require the two counts kept apart. The split did not remove them from the completion condition and the plan does not drop them.

decisions.summary: Each of the fifty-one Sources lines carrying a disclosure a note now holds is rewritten to point at the note, with no change of meaning, followed by make citations and the footnote tests.
decisions.why: FR-013 and D5 make these work rather than a second deferral.

decisions.summary: The closing report in research.md: per page what closed in each of the three forms, per unclosed item searched-and-failed or never-searched, the two settled items named, and the two counts reported separately.
decisions.why: FR-011, SC-009 and SC-013 require each part.

decisions.summary: The 'A page the container cannot fetch is not thereby unreadable' paragraph in the skill's research CLAUDE.md gains the download-list rule in the FR-010 shape with the GM's reason quoted and the plain statement that no gate here reads the list, and the root CLAUDE.md's citation rule gains a pointer.
decisions.why: FR-015 and SC-015 name both files and every part; the GM asked for the guidelines to carry the format 'in the future, anytime'.

decisions.summary: The guidelines paragraph is written BEFORE the first Part 4 entry is appended, so this feature's own hand-over is the first under the rule.
decisions.why: An ordering inside work the spec already requires; it removes no obligation.

decisions.summary: At the close, the check reports are applied where they bear on honesty - every quote-check NOT-ON-PAGE, DOES-NOT-SUPPORT, MISPLACED and DIFFERS verdict, every reader-visible defect and untranslated quotation the record-format reports name, the batch-1 applicability corrections - and the rest is named to feature 250.
decisions.why: The GM made this cut themselves on 2026-09-14 (request.md: 'this feature is too big ... with the rest deferred to a future feature', then 'Yes that does suit me, please do that'), and the cut they accepted names these four classes as applied and the cosmetic record-format findings as deferred. The plan's enumeration is that list item for item, so nothing is carved out contrary to what was asked; spec D7 and FR-011 carry the same cut.

decisions.summary: The confirmation after the correction edits is one quote-check and one record-format per edited page, each given the changed notes and sections rather than the whole page, because the page was already checked whole.
decisions.why: The GM's accepted cut says 're-check once, scoped to the changed notes and sections' in those words, and the amended FR-007 carries it with the limit that a page checked whole for the first time is still checked whole. The plan states that limit's premise (the page was already checked whole), so it does not extend the scoping to an unchecked page.

decisions.summary: The entry-drift pairs are answered by measurement: measure/prose_moved.py classifies every moved section MARKS-ONLY or WORDING-MOVED, entry-drift is dispatched at every named pair with a WORDING-MOVED section and DRIFTED prose is rewritten, and the MARKS-ONLY pairs are discharged with one recorded ENTRY_DRIFT_OK citing the measurement.
decisions.why: The GM's accepted cut says 'answer the entry-drift pairs by measuring which sections' wording moved'; FR-008 already permits either a dispatch or one recorded waiver over a sweep in which no finding moved, and MARKS-ONLY is that condition measured rather than asserted. D8 and SC-016 carry it.

decisions.summary: cities/sizing.html is not footnoted here; T16 is removed from tasks.md and the page becomes feature 250's FR-001.
decisions.why: The sizing page is the first item on the GM's own accepted deferral list in request.md, and spec D7 and FR-011 name it. Deferring it is the ruling being carried out, not a carve-out against it.
